title: SG-7.3 · Implement the execution runner in worker/internal
summary: Execution runner takes the per-World lock, runs the agent in an isolated worktree with timeout, retries, budget stop and approval gate
description: Context: backend/worker has config, lock (lock.Acquire/ErrLocked) and store (store.Store, Execution, Status) packages but no runner. Desired behavior: a runner package that locks, runs an agent in an isolated worktree under a context timeout, retries up to the configured limit, stops when budget is exceeded and blocks at the approval gate before publishing unless auto-publish is on. Expected result: Runner.Run drives one execution to COMPLETED, AWAITING_APPROVAL or FAILED. Why: the worker must never corrupt production and must run one execution per World.
acceptance_criteria: Given the lock file exists, when Run is called, then it returns an error satisfying errors.Is(err, lock.ErrLocked) and neither the worktree nor the agent is touched
Given an agent that blocks, when the timeout elapses, then Run returns context.DeadlineExceeded and the execution is FAILED
Given an agent failing twice then succeeding and MaxRetries 2, when Run is called, then the agent runs 3 times and the execution is not FAILED
Given the accumulated cost exceeds MaxBudget, when an attempt finishes, then Run stops retrying and returns ErrBudgetExceeded
Given AutoPublish is false and the agent succeeds, then the status is AWAITING_APPROVAL and Publish is not called; when true, Publish is called and status is COMPLETED

out_of_scope: real git worktree and Claude provider implementations
preserve: lock, store and config package APIs

technical_constraints: Go 1.22, standard library only plus existing packages
Agent, Worktrees and Publisher are interfaces so tests use fakes
definition_of_done: All acceptance criteria are met by runner package code
non_functional: No shell interpolation of any prompt text
